instruction: Commit the binder project files with message "version 1.0" and push to the remote repository on the main branch.

command: git config --global user.name "xlang" && git config --global user.email "xlang2024anonym@gmail.com" && mkdir -p /home/user/projects/remote_project && cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git init --initial-branch=main && git config receive.denyCurrentBranch ignore
unzip -q /home/user/Downloads/binder.zip -d /home/user/projects/ && cd /home/user/projects/binder && git init --initial-branch main && git remote add origin /home/user/projects/remote_project

cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {printf "%s%s", $i, (i==NF ? "" : " ")}; print ""}'; remote_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); cd /home/user/projects/binder && local_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); if [ "${local_id}" = "${remote_id}" ]; then echo "repo is synchronous"; else echo "repo is not synchronous"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires staging all files, committing with message 'version 1.0', and pushing to remote main. The evaluator verifies the commit message in remote and checks synchronization between local and remote repositories.
metadata.verification: Tested evaluator logic: Command extracts commit message from remote repository and verifies local/remote commit IDs match.

Correct state extraction: Command correctly navigates to remote repo, extracts commit message from git log, and compares commit IDs between local and remote
Logical correctness: Synchronization check ensures push was successful by comparing local/remote commit IDs
Practical feasibility: The vm_command_line getter can execute the multi-step bash command and extract output correctly
Correct metric usage: check_include_exclude with both 'version 1.0' and 'repo is synchronous' ensures both conditions must be met
Edge cases handled: Failed push results in 'repo is not synchronous', wrong commit message fails the check
